items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: There were some nice musicians in Alex's orchestra and I became acquainted with ... Joldie

ctx.x: They made a big hit with the women, and wherever the women went, the men were sure to be there. So Alex stayed in the vicinity of Cincinnati for months and even worked at a white open air dancing place on Vine Street in Walnut Hills where no other negro orchestra had ever worked. Walnut Hills is a suburb of Cincinnati.

There were some nice musicians in Alex's orchestra and I became acquainted with Leonard Fields who had a technique like Rudy Wedolf on alto sax, Clarence Wheeler, who was the first trumpet man and Joldie whose last name I don't remember, who played a growl style of trumpet like Nassau whom I had worked with in the Clarence Paige orchestra.
